summary: Teams of 2-4 students build a database-driven web application for a student-to-professional mentorship platform, including user registration, mentor/mentee profiles, session booking, and admin controls. The project is submitted online as a combined PDF with supporting materials and source code, followed by a virtual presentation to judges. Teams are scored on technical implementation, design, database integration, security, and presentation quality.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: One combined PDF file containing the URL to the database driven website, written description of the application, source code, and the database schema, Works Cited (formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual), BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Source code (as a zipped root folder)
presubmit_items: Clickable URL to Database Driven Website
Written description of the project, source code, and the database schema
deadlines: Event registration deadline is no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
National submission deadline: January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
competencies: Design and implement a database in a structured (SQL) or unstructured (cloud-based, e.g., MongoDB, Firebase) environment to store and manage application data; flat files may not be used for data storage
Demonstrate knowledge of server-side scripting and Internet concepts to support dynamic, functional web application behavior
Evaluate project requirements and delegate responsibilities effectively within a team, demonstrating the collaboration and communication skills required in a professional business setting
Integrate external Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to extend application functionality and connect to third-party services and data sources
Apply back-end database development skills and front-end web design standards to build a complete, functional, and visually consistent full-stack web application
Implement structured problem-solving techniques to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve technical challenges throughout the development process
Document the process, methodology, and lifecycle of the web application, including an audit trail that demonstrates how the application was planned, built, and iterated

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Layout is highly intuitive and visually engaging, enhancing user understanding through excellent design principles.
Colors and fonts are expertly selected and harmonized, enhancing the overall aesthetic and user experience.
Images and files are expertly optimized, ensuring fast load times and excellent performance across devices.
Writing is polished, engaging, and consistently well-structured with excellent clarity and style.
Contrast is strong and thoughtfully applied, enhancing readability and visual appeal.
Links are fully functional, consistent, and enhance navigation.
Instructions are clear and feedback is timely and user-friendly.
Site performs seamlessly and consistently on all platforms.
Search is efficient, accurate, and user-friendly.
Database is well-integrated and enhances performance.
Model is well-executed and clearly supports the app’s structure.
Tables are well-normalized with no unnecessary repetition.
Encryption is thorough and enhances security.
Strong access controls ensure secure, role-based access.
Unique keys are well-structured and optimize data integrity.
Diagram is detailed, well-integrated into the development process, and enhances understanding of system architecture.
State management is robust, secure, and gracefully manages both cookie and non-cookie scenarios.
Encryption is implemented using strong, up-to-date algorithms and integrated seamlessly into the system’s security architecture.
Validation is thorough, user-friendly, and includes both client-side and server-side checks.
Queries and stored procedures are optimized, secure, and demonstrate thoughtful database design.
Error handling is comprehensive, user-friendly, and anticipates edge cases to maintain system reliability.
Reports are well-designed and enhance understanding through dynamic visuals and interactivity.
Admin interface is secure, intuitive, and supports efficient data management with role-based access or audit features.
Documentation is thorough, consistent, and enhances readability and maintainability across the codebase.
Reports are highly accurate, validated against multiple data sources, and reliably reflect real-time or complex data scenarios.
Content visibility is well-integrated, secure, and includes intuitive controls or role-based access features.
Admin functions are fully operational, intuitive, and include safeguards like confirmation prompts or audit logging.
Security is robust, proactively mitigates vulnerabilities, and includes advanced features like encryption, role-based access, and audit logging.
Required features are fully functional, secure, and enhanced with thoughtful design (e.g., role-based access, password hashing, user-friendly interfaces).

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Clearly explains the process, including key decisions, challenges, and solutions.
Demonstration is smooth, engaging, and highlights full functionality through intuitive use of the user interface.
Provides a clear, insightful explanation of the logical design and effectively links design patterns to application decisions.
Delivers accurate insights into code architecture, clearly connects front-end and back-end logic, and responds confidently to follow-up questions.
Delivers concise, well-structured, and insightful responses; demonstrates strong communication skills and a deep understanding of the topic.
Consistently accurate and polished use of grammar, spelling, punctuation, and usage; enhances clarity and professionalism.
Presentation is polished, confident, and highly engaging; demonstrates strong delivery, visual clarity, and audience awareness.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
Advisors of qualifying teams will be contacted to reserve a time for a videoconference presentation before a panel of judges.
Teams will be assigned to sections prior to the preliminary presentation.
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.
Teams who do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines will be disqualified.
Teams participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible.
Only the team captain should complete the submission.
